originalTitle: A finite-sum Lyapunov function for a stocked Ricker map
abstract: We consider the fixed planar map T (x, y) = (x exp(3/2 − y) + e − 1, x), an example in the literature on delayed Ricker models with stocking. Every positive original phase enters an explicit invariant rectangle after thirty iterates. A positive quadratic function contracts there after five iterates, as proved by a finite exact-integer interval certificate and an analytic local estimate. A weighted sum of thirty-five evaluations of that quadratic function is then a real analytic, coercive state Lyapunov function with strict decrease on the entire positive quadrant. This proves global asymptotic stability, square summability of the phase error and an explicit local-entry bound. We also prove that no centered constant positive-definite quadratic can be nonincreasing at every step on the source-associated invariant square. The finite-step conversion and rigorous verification tools are classical; the result is a quantitative verification for this one prescribed map.

originalTitle: An explicit capture energy for a critical polarized Duffing map
abstract: We give an explicit phase energy for the critical polarization of a linearly implicit two-step Duffing scheme. The inherited polarized energy controls the product of the two positions and both momenta, but its sublevels are noncompact. A corrected position imbalance supplies the missing control. On each fixed polarized-energy cap, the absolute imbalance has a one-sided increment bound obtained before either position is known to be bounded. Adding it to the inherited energy gives compact invariant sublevels for every positive step and damping parameter and every independent initial pair. A sum over two phase iterates is strictly decreasing outside the full stationary-pair set. Finite variation of the imbalance then selects one stationary pair; in the original indices, distinct even and odd limits are possible. The recurrence, polarized dissipation and finite-step Lyapunov principles have established antecedents. The result is confined to this critical map, and close-source access limitations are stated explicitly.

originalTitle: A finite-history Lyapunov function at the BDF3 semiconvexity endpoint
abstract: We consider fully implicit BDF3 for a globally finite, coercive C^{1} potential F on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, where F + (c/2)∥·∥^{2} is convex and hc = 95/48. Every root of each implicit equation is allowed, from an arbitrary initial triple. Pierre’s endpoint quadratic identity gives a nonincreasing modified energy with a semidefinite loss. We show that three consecutive zero losses along an actual BDF3 segment force its six points to coincide at a critical point. Summing three modified energies therefore gives an explicit transition-strict Lyapunov function on internally admissible five-point histories. Compactness and closedness of the original relation then imply asymptotic regularity and a compact connected critical omega-limit set at one value of F , for every root selection. The conclusion is critical-set capture; convergence to a single point is not asserted. The comparison with previous work is restricted to the explicitly cited preprint versions.

originalTitle: Explicit convergence certificates for Chambolle–Pock at small extrapolation
abstract: We give explicit convergence certificates for two small extrapolation parameters of the unmodified Chambolle–Pock method. At θ = 1/4, an integer quadratic energy on three consecutive states proves weak convergence whenever τ σ∥L∥^{2} ≤ 5/2. The certificate applies to arbitrary bounded linear coupling between real Hilbert spaces, proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions, and arbitrary initial points. It also gives square-summable increments and a summable saddle gap. Its positivity uses the actual proximal history, and all matrix inequalities are certified by exact rational arithmetic. At θ = 1/2, a finite-window argument completes the weak-convergence consequence of a previously published energy throughout τ σ∥L∥^{2} < 2. This latter range meets the known bilinear obstruction. The quarter-extrapolation bound is not asserted to be optimal.

originalTitle: Exact planar Chambolle–Pock three-cycles and an optimal ordered triangle family
abstract: For every nonnegative extrapolation parameter, we construct an exact period-three orbit of the literal primal-first Chambolle–Pock map using two triangles in ordinary Euclidean space. We determine the smallest stepsize product admitting the prescribed orbit within an explicitly restricted ordered equilateral-triangle class. The proof reduces the projection conditions to four scalar inequalities and an exact ellipse support calculation. At extrapolation 1/8, the product is (88 + 16√91)/81 ≈ 2.970744, below the quadratic benchmark 16/5. More generally, the family lies below that benchmark on an exact interval of extrapolation parameters. The result does not determine the universal convex convergence threshold. No novelty claim is made.

originalTitle: Exact classification of regular star polygon Chambolle–Pock cycles
abstract: We classify the stepsize products of paired regular polygon cycles traversed with a coprime star step under the literal Euclidean primal-first Chambolle–Pock map. Positive extrapolation permits only maximal stars of odd order; their exact attained minimum increases strictly with the order and exceeds the triangle minimum. Every larger product is feasible with the same minimizing dual vertex. At zero extrapolation, other star steps also occur, and some improve the triangle and bilinear cycle products. We give their complete classification, prove all vertex normal inequalities analytically, and distinguish geometric polygon edges from traversal chords. The result concerns a fixed-rotation/scaling ansatz and is not a universal convergence theorem. No novelty claim is made.

originalTitle: A finite-history Lyapunov function for geodesic inertial proximal trajectories
abstract: We study an inertial proximal recurrence on a Hadamard manifold of finite dimension and globally lower-bounded sectional curvature. For a proper lower semi-continuous geodesically convex objective with an attained minimum, every constant inertia in [0, 1) and every positive proximal parameter admit an explicit Lyapunov function of the current two-point phase and objective value. Its coercivity and one-step descent bound every trajectory from arbitrary initial points, without coercivity of the objective or boundedness of its minimizer set. The same energy proves square summability of the increments and convergence to one minimizer. A regularized distance with globally bounded Hessian supplies the geometric term, and no future trajectory terms are used. Classical ingredients, Euclidean ancestry and unresolved comparisons with nearby literature are identified.

originalTitle: Conditional compact-manifold capture for the original-clock IGATH-2 recursion
abstract: We prove a conditional capture theorem for a fixed-parameter IGATH-2 recursion near a compact normally nondegenerate manifold of local minima. The manifold and objective are both of class C^{5}, and the normal Hessian spectrum lies in a fixed compact subinterval of (0, 4). An independent history pair may enter at any sufficiently late original index, with uniformly small scaled normal position and current-base normal history and with any prescribed finite scaled tangent-history bound. The resulting suffix remains in a controlled tube, has finite quadratic slow-clock dissipation, and approaches the critical set of the squared norm restricted to the manifold. A discrete two-history contraction retains the entry transient, a strict discrete energy closes the capture bootstrap, and a curvature-dependent frozen target is derived and tracked to order k^{−3/2}. This is a newly formulated C^{5}/C^{5} theorem. No convergence to one point, finite total travel, arbitrary early capture, or globally least-norm selection is asserted.

originalTitle: Split curvature and convergence of B-adaPG with flat boundary kernels
abstract: We prove convergence of the original undamped adaptive Bregman proximal-gradient method under additional curvature in the finite proximal term. The kernel may have a flat boundary face through the optimizer. The proximal term is only required to be strictly convex on the feasible set, with no strong-convexity modulus; the differentiable term may be nonlinear, but its relative smoothness must be uniform on bounded interior sets approaching the boundary. Retaining a nonsmooth slack in the exact merit identity gives separation through compact midpoint gaps. Divergence of cumulative selected stepsizes and a small-step/large-step argument then imply objective and point convergence for arbitrary positive initialization. A nonlinear example verifies the assumptions with a flat kernel face. The unrestricted unique-minimizer boundary problem remains unresolved.

originalTitle: A discrete Lyapunov certificate for an aggressive weak-gradient iteration
abstract: We verify a discrete Lyapunov estimate for the aggressive weak-gradient iteration of Ushiyama, Sato and Matsuo. The method and its energy are inherited. For a globally smooth strongly convex potential, an exact one-step identity gives an explicit sufficient step interval, geometric energy decay and weighted dissipation. The energy controls both original phase coordinates despite its negative quadratic term. Consequently every independent initial phase converges geometrically to the equilibrium. The upper-step equality and equal smoothness and convexity constants are included. The proof supplies the discrete coefficient calculation and initialization scope for this printed map; it makes no maximal-range or method-priority claim.

originalTitle: Two-step Lyapunov decrease at a logarithmic boundary for a nonconvex Douglas–Rachford iteration
abstract: We consider the Douglas–Rachford relation for a union of two affine lines and a third line, retaining every nearest-line projection at a tie. At the nonperpendicular logarithmic equality boundary of the product-energy criterion of Giladi and Rüffer, their product energy is nonincreasing but has nonfeasible equality transitions. We determine all such transitions: each affine branch has one contact on a projection bisector, and no equality successor is another equality input. Consequently the same product energy decreases strictly along every two-step path starting outside the feasible pair. Its properness and the closed graph of the full relation imply boundedness, decay of the energy to zero, and approach to the feasible pair for every trajectory. The argument uses exact contact geometry and a compact three-point limit passage.

originalTitle: Strict quadratic Lyapunov decay for a torus map
abstract: Buescu and Oliveira proposed a piecewise quadratic Lyapunov function for a torus map arising from three coupled clocks. We verify strict decrease of this exact function for every parameter 0 < a < 1/3. In circular-gap coordinates, the function is a centered sum of three squares. The update does not decrease the smallest gap or increase the largest gap, and it preserves their order. An elementary three-coordinate majorization argument then gives a one-step energy loss of at least half the squared gap displacement. The formulas agree across the torus seams, and the loss vanishes exactly at the six fixed points. This verifies a strict-decrease property of the proposed function; Conley completeness is a separate requirement.

originalTitle: An exact period-three Chambolle–Pock orbit at θ = 1/8 below the quadratic threshold
abstract: We give a rational four-dimensional convex projection example for the literal primal-first Chambolle–Pock map with extrapolation θ = 1/8. The stepsize product is 3, strictly below the quadratic benchmark 16/5, yet an explicitly initialized orbit has exact period three. A positive definite rational Gram matrix and two triangles specify the entire instance. All projection optimality conditions are verified by finite tables of rational inner products. The example disproves the proposed universal convex extension of that benchmark, not a published convergence theorem. It is bounded, its ordinary averages converge to a saddle point, and it does not determine the sharp universal threshold. The construction transfers isometrically to ordinary Euclidean space. A standalone exact-arithmetic verifier accompanies the proof. No novelty claim is made.

originalTitle: Exact classification of ordered regular polygon Chambolle–Pock cycles
abstract: We classify exact paired regular polygon cycles of the literal primal-first Chambolle–Pock map in the ordinary Euclidean plane. For every integer m ≥ 4, positive extrapolation excludes the prescribed ordered regular m-gon orbit at every positive stepsize product. At zero extrapolation, m ≥ 5 admits exactly one product and one dual vertex, whereas the square admits an explicit exceptional family. The proof establishes the equivalence of all vertex normal inequalities to four adjacent tests, including every boundary case. The zero-extrapolation minima are 4 sin^{2}(π/m), with unattained infimum zero over finite polygons. These are restricted-class statements, not a classification of arbitrary cycles or a universal convergence theorem. No novelty claim is made.

originalTitle: A forward quadratic on a flat-boundary kernel: structural conclusions for the exact B-adaPG controller
abstract: We analyze the original undamped, full-ambient B-adaPG method on an oscillatory Legendre kernel that is constant on a boundary edge, with a quadratic tangential term placed entirely in the forward objective. For every interior initialization and every pair of positive initial stepsizes, cumulative steps diverge, the normal coordinate has an exact cumulative-step asymptotic, and the squared tangential coordinate is summable with outgoing-step weights. The unique minimizer is a cluster point, and every subsequence with outgoing steps bounded away from zero converges to it. Boundary-uniform relative smoothness genuinely fails, although compact-interior relative smoothness holds. These are structural partial conclusions: neither full point or objective convergence, nor a divergent orbit, nor eventual selection of a controller branch is established. A finite high-precision illustration is separated from the proofs. No novelty claim is made.

originalTitle: Sharp convergence regions and periodic obstructions for Chambolle–Pock
abstract: For the literal primal-first Chambolle–Pock iteration, we prove the sharp universal strict product cap R_{3}(θ) = (√(4 + 12θ + 12θ^{2}) + 1 + 3θ)/(1 + θ)^{2} on two explicit closed extrapolation intervals, one containing 1/8 and one containing 1/7, with a separate exact result at 11/74. For fixed proper lower-semicontinuous convex objectives on arbitrary real Hilbert spaces, bounded linear coupling, nonempty KKT set and arbitrary initialization, every strict product below this curve gives bounded whole-sequence weak convergence, square-summable increments and strongly vanishing KKT residuals. Convergence is in norm in finite dimensions. Exact rational storage families and continuous Bernstein–Gershgorin bounds certify the two regions; contraction embedding covers every smaller product. The complete original 1/8 proof and its coefficientwise recovery are retained. For all θ ≥ 0, the same curve is the exact minimum product for an actual nonconstant three-periodic orbit, with an explicit fixed-triangle realization. Nevertheless, two fixed indicator functions in R^{4}, with a unique KKT pair, admit a least-period-five orbit at θ = 9/50, product 147/50, strictly below both this curve and the bilinear period-two obstruction. The same states and hulls work on an explicit parameter rectangle. Thus period-two and period-three obstructions alone do not determine the full convergence boundary. The claims are supported by exact data and independent solver-free replays; neither a complete extrapolation classification nor endpoint convergence is asserted. On [177/1000, 183/1000], we further identify the exact five-cycle onset as an analytic algebraic branch. Two unique transverse crossings delimit precisely where it preempts periods two through four, and every normalized endpoint moment vector is the same saturated two-frequency vector.

originalTitle: Growth and boundedness at the critical Chambolle–Pock endpoint
abstract: At extrapolation 1/8 and step product r_{∗} = (88 + 16√91)/81, the literal primal-first Chambolle–Pock method has bounded increments but need not have bounded positions. We give a coherent account of this critical dynamics. An exact semicoercive certificate bounds the increments of every initialized Hilbert-space orbit. A signed storage then proves an explicit O(√N ) maximal-radius estimate whenever a KKT pair exists; the storage theorem itself holds at all positive steps and every real extrapolation parameter under bounded increments. A single explicit endpoint orbit has compact dual set, unique KKT pair, and primal norm at least √n/[16(1+log_{4} n)] at every positive time. The construction establishes sharpness only of the universal polynomial exponent. Bounded dual domain together with primal-objective coercivity restores boundedness at all positive steps and nonnegative extrapolation, with quantitative interior-ball and finite-dimensional consequences. We also retain boundedness for eventual periodic affine itineraries and a no-drift obstruction for arbitrary monotone graphs. These results separate unique solvability, coercivity, and finite-dimensional structure; general nonseparable finite-dimensional endpoint boundedness remains open.

originalTitle: Scalar order and separable convergence for primal-first Chambolle–Pock
abstract: Scalar order strengthens primal-first Chambolle–Pock at extrapolation 1/8. For countably scalar-separable objectives in matched diagonal coordinates, KKT existence gives strong paired convergence through r_{∗} = (88+16√91)/81 and a summable coordinate envelope with squared constant 10^{20}, including zero and arbitrarily small couplings. We make scalar continuation effective with η_{eff} = 10^{−118}. A genuine finite-shadow state Lyapunov function then gives whole-orbit KKT convergence and square-summable actual increments for scalar parameters r_{n} ∈ [m, r_{∗} + η_{eff}], m > 0, of finite total variation, also with summable full-state errors or the stated two-proximal-output errors. The objectives remain fixed; no smallness of variation or total error is required. The proof combines exact four-output order, robust anchored axis geometry, positive finite-shadow energies and an overlapping parameter partition. The original fixed-step matched-Hilbert extension and its envelope max{10^{20}, 3B^{2}_{cont}} are retained with complete proofs. Separately, every scalar orbit whose period divides six is constant when 297/100 ≤ r < 3, without a KKT assumption; four- and five-period exclusions force every nonconstant periodic orbit there to have least period at least seven. We retain all-real-extrapolation trapping and the complete period-three classification for nonnegative extrapolation. The explicit extension is an effective existence result. No convergence rate, uniform robustness as m ↓ 0, variable-parameter Hilbert theorem, or convergence throughout (r_{∗}, 3) is asserted. Complete analytic proofs and solver-free finite verification data are supplied.
